# Book III, Proposition 32

*Angles with the tangent equal those in the alternate segments*

[Euclid's proof](#euclids-proof) · [In Lean](#in-lean) · [What it rests on](#what-it-rests-on) · [Mishnah](#mishnah)

> If a straight line touch a circle, and from the point of contact there be drawn across, in the circle, a straight line cutting the circle, the angles which it makes with the tangent will be equal to the angles in the alternate segments of the circle.

**In Lean:** ✅ proved, as Euclid states it · Euclid's argument

## Euclid's proof

<p align="center"><img src="../../figures/III/32.svg" alt="Euclid's figure for Proposition III.32, with Heath's letters. Drawn for one case: D on F's side of BA and apart from A, as in Heath's figure." width="360"></p>

<p align="center"><em>Drawn for one case: D on F's side of BA and apart from A, as in Heath's figure.</em></p>

For let a straight line EF touch the circle ABCD at the point B, and from the point B let there be drawn across, in the circle ABCD, a straight line BD cutting it;

I say that the angles which BD makes with the tangent EF will be equal to the angles in the alternate segments of the circle, that is, that the angle FBD is equal to the angle constructed in the segment BAD, and the angle EBD is equal to the angle constructed in the segment DCB.

For let BA be drawn from B at right angles to EF,

let a point C be taken at random on the circumference BD,

and let AD, DC, CB be joined.

Then, since a straight line EF touches the circle ABCD at B,

and BA has been drawn from the point of contact at right angles to the tangent,

the centre of the circle ABCD is on BA. [III. 19]

Therefore BA is a diameter of the circle ABCD;

therefore the angle ADB, being an angle in a semicircle, is right. [III. 31]

Therefore the remaining angles BAD, ABD are equal to one right angle. [I. 32]

But the angle ABF is also right;

therefore the angle ABF is equal to the angles BAD, ABD.

Let the angle ABD be subtracted from each;

therefore the angle DBF which remains is equal to the angle BAD in the alternate segment of the circle.

Next, since ABCD is a quadrilateral in a circle,

its opposite angles are equal to two right angles. [III. 22]

But the angles DBF, DBE are also equal to two right angles;

therefore the angles DBF, DBE are equal to the angles BAD, BCD,

of which the angle BAD was proved equal to the angle DBF;

therefore the angle DBE which remains is equal to the angle DCB in the alternate segment DCB of the circle.

Therefore etc.

Q. E. D.

The list below marks where a lemma does a step Euclid takes for granted, where the Lean takes a case Euclid's figure leaves aside and where the statement already gives a step; the `/- … -/` notes in the listing explain smaller adjustments.

**How the Lean follows the text**

- **Already given.** "let a point C be taken at random on the circumference BD…" The statement's second conclusion is said of every point C of the segment DCB, so C comes with it; the Lean takes C up where that conclusion is proved.
- **Done by `Prop32.sameSide`.** "Therefore BA is a diameter of the circle ABCD…" Euclid takes for granted that A and D lie on one side of EF; the Lean proves it: on opposite sides, AD would cross EF within the circle (III.2), and no point of a straight line touching a circle is within it, as in III.18.
- **A further case.** "therefore the angle ADB, being an angle in a semicircle, is right." When D is A, BD is itself the diameter and there is no triangle ABD: every angle in either segment is right by III.31, as are the angles FBD and EBD.
- **A further case.** "Let the angle ABD be subtracted from each…" Euclid's figure has D on F's side of BA, within the angle ABF; when D is on E's side, the Lean gives the same argument with E and F exchanged.
- **A further case.** "therefore the angle DBF which remains…" Euclid's A is the end of the diameter; the statement says this of every point of the segment BAD, and III.21 makes each such angle equal to BAD.

```lean
/-- Two points of a circle, neither of them the point B where the straight line EF
touches it, lie on the same side of EF. Euclid takes this for granted. Were they on
opposite sides, the straight line joining them would cross EF at a point within the
circle by III.2, and no point of a straight line touching a circle is within
it, as in III.18. -/
theorem Prop32.sameSide {B E F P Q : Point} {α : Circle} {L : Line}
    (hα : ∃ O : Point, Centre O α) (hEF : Touches E F α)
    (hE_L : OnLine E L) (hF_L : OnLine F L) (hB_L : OnLine B L) (hB : OnCircle B α)
    (hP : OnCircle P α) (hQ : OnCircle Q α) (hPB : P ≠ B) (hQB : Q ≠ B) : SameSide P Q L := by
  have off : ∀ {R : Point}, OnCircle R α → R ≠ B → ¬ OnLine R L := fun hR hRB h =>
    (hEF.2 L hE_L hF_L).2 ⟨B, _, hRB.symm, hB_L, hB, h, hR⟩
  refine Classical.byContradiction fun hs => ?_
  obtain ⟨Y, hY_L, hPYQ⟩ := OppositeSides.exists_between ⟨off hP hPB, off hQ hQB, hs⟩
  exact hEF.not_inside ⟨L, hE_L, hF_L, hY_L⟩ (Prop2 hα hP hQ Y hPYQ)
```

```lean
/-- If a straight line touch a circle, and from the point of contact there be drawn across, in the
circle, a straight line cutting the circle, the angles which it makes with the tangent will be
equal to the angles in the alternate segments of the circle. -/
theorem Prop32 {B D E F : Point} {ABCD : Circle} (hABCD : ∃ O : Point, Centre O ABCD)
    (hB : OnCircle B ABCD) (hD : OnCircle D ABCD) (hBD : B ≠ D) (hEF : Touches E F ABCD)
    (hEBF : Between E B F) :
    (∀ A : Point, OnCircle A ABCD → OppositeSidesOf A F B D → ∠ F B D = ∠ B A D) ∧
    (∀ C : Point, OnCircle C ABCD → SameSideOf C F B D → ∠ E B D = ∠ D C B) := by
  -- For let a straight line EF touch the circle ABCD at the point B, and from the point B let
  -- there be drawn across, in the circle ABCD, a straight line BD cutting it;
  have hEF' : E ≠ F := ne_of_between_ends hEBF
  obtain ⟨L, hE_L, hF_L⟩ := Postulate1 E F hEF'
  have hB_L : OnLine B L := on_line_of_between_ends hEBF hE_L hF_L
  have onL : ∀ {P : Point}, Collinear E F P → OnLine P L := fun ⟨M, h1, h2, h3⟩ =>
    (line_unique hEF' h1 h2 hE_L hF_L) ▸ h3
  have off : ∀ {R : Point}, OnCircle R ABCD → R ≠ B → ¬ OnLine R L := fun hR hRB h =>
    (hEF.2 L hE_L hF_L).2 ⟨B, _, hRB.symm, hB_L, hB, h, hR⟩
  have hD_L : ¬ OnLine D L := off hD hBD.symm
  -- I say that the angles which BD makes with the tangent EF will be equal to the angles in
  -- the alternate segments of the circle, that is, that the angle FBD is equal to the angle
  -- constructed in the segment BAD, and the angle EBD is equal to the angle constructed in the
  -- segment DCB.
  -- For let BA be drawn from B at right angles to EF,
  obtain ⟨X, hXD, hX⟩ := BookI.Prop11 hEF' ⟨L, hE_L, hF_L, hB_L⟩ (fun h => hD_L (onL h))
  have hX_L : ¬ OnLine X L := not_on_line_of_same_side (hXD.sameSide hE_L hF_L)
  have hXB : X ≠ B := fun e => hX_L (e ▸ hB_L)
  -- let a point C be taken at random on the circumference BD,
  /- The second conclusion takes any such C, and we bring C in when we prove it, below. -/
  -- and let AD, DC, CB be joined.
  -- Then, since a straight line EF touches the circle ABCD at B,
  -- and BA has been drawn from the point of contact at right angles to the tangent,
  -- the centre of the circle ABCD is on BA. [III. 19]
  obtain ⟨O, hO⟩ := hABCD
  have hXBO : Collinear X B O :=
    Prop19 hB hEF ⟨L, hE_L, hF_L, hB_L⟩ (fun h => hX_L (onL h))
      (fun P hP hPB => (angle_symm hXB hPB).trans (hX P hP hPB)) O hO
  -- Therefore BA is a diameter of the circle ABCD;
  obtain ⟨M, hX_M, hB_M, hO_M⟩ := hXBO
  obtain ⟨A, hA, hA_M, hAOB⟩ :=
    line_circle_beyond (centre_inside hO) hO_M hB_M (ne_of_centre_of_on hO hB)
  have hAB : A ≠ B := ne_of_between_ends hAOB
  /- A is on X's side of EF, the side of the circle, so the straight line BA is the one
     drawn at right angles to EF. -/
  have hAD_L : SameSide A D L :=
    Prop32.sameSide ⟨O, hO⟩ hEF hE_L hF_L hB_L hB hA hD hAB hBD.symm
  have hAX : OnRay A B X :=
    OnRay.of_sameSideOf (E := F) (SameSideOf.of_line (ne_of_between (between_symm hEBF)).symm
      hB_L hF_L (same_side_trans (same_side_symm hAD_L) (same_side_symm (hXD.sameSide hE_L hF_L))))
      ⟨M, hB_M, hX_M, hA_M⟩ hAB
  have hright : ∀ {P : Point}, OnLine P L → P ≠ B → ∠ A B P = ∟ := fun hP hPB => by
    rw [angle_symm hAB hPB, angle_onRay_right hAX hPB]
    exact hX _ ⟨L, hE_L, hF_L, hP⟩ hPB
  /- Euclid's figure has D on F's side of BA. We write the rest of his argument once, for
     whichever end of the tangent is on D's side, and take the case of D at A at the end. -/
  have key : ∀ {E F : Point}, Between E B F → OnLine E L → OnLine F L → SameSideOf D F B A →
      (∀ A' : Point, OnCircle A' ABCD → OppositeSidesOf A' F B D → ∠ F B D = ∠ B A' D) ∧
      (∀ C : Point, OnCircle C ABCD → SameSideOf C F B D → ∠ E B D = ∠ D C B) := by
    intro E F hEBF hE_L hF_L hDF
    have hFB : F ≠ B := (ne_of_between (between_symm hEBF))
    have hBAD : Triangle B A D := hDF.triangle
    -- therefore the angle ADB, being an angle in a semicircle, is right. [III. 31]
    have hADB : ∠ A D B = ∟ := (Prop31 hO hD hA hB hAOB hBAD.ne₂₃.symm hBD.symm).1
    -- Therefore the remaining angles BAD, ABD are equal to one right angle. [I. 32]
    obtain ⟨P, hADP⟩ := produce hBAD.ne₂₃
    have h32 := (BookI.Prop32 hBAD hADP).2
    rw [hADB, add_comm (∠ B A D) ∟, add_assoc, add_comm ∟,
      angle_symm hBD.symm hAB] at h32
    have hrem : ∠ B A D + ∠ A B D = ∟ := CommonNotion3 h32 rfl
    -- But the angle ABF is also right;
    have hABF : ∠ A B F = ∟ := hright hF_L hFB
    -- therefore the angle ABF is equal to the angles BAD, ABD.
    have h1 : ∠ A B F = ∠ B A D + ∠ A B D := hABF.trans hrem.symm
    -- Let the angle ABD be subtracted from each;
    have hDA_F : SameSideOf D A B F :=
      SameSideOf.of_line hFB.symm hB_L hF_L (same_side_symm hAD_L)
    have hsplit : ∠ A B F = ∠ A B D + ∠ D B F := angle_add_of_within hDF hDA_F
    -- therefore the angle DBF which remains is equal to the angle BAD in the alternate segment
    -- of the circle.
    have hDBF : ∠ D B F = ∠ B A D := CommonNotion3 (by rw [add_comm, ← hsplit, h1]) rfl
    /- A is on the other side of BD from F, for the straight line BD, within the angle
       ABF, crosses AF. -/
    obtain ⟨N, hB_N, hD_N⟩ := Postulate1 B D hBD
    obtain ⟨Y, hAYF, hY⟩ := crossbar hDF hDA_F
    obtain ⟨-, -, ⟨N', hB_N', hD_N', hY_N'⟩, -⟩ := hY
    have hY_N : OnLine Y N := (line_unique hBD hB_N' hD_N' hB_N hD_N) ▸ hY_N'
    have hF_N : ¬ OnLine F N := fun h =>
      hD_L ((line_unique hFB.symm hB_N h hB_L hF_L) ▸ hD_N)
    have hAF : OppositeSidesOf A F B D :=
      OppositeSidesOf.of_line hBD hB_N hD_N
        ⟨(Prop2.triangle ⟨O, hO⟩ hB hD hA hBD hBAD.ne₂₃.symm hAB.symm).off_line hB_N hD_N,
          hF_N, pasch3 hAYF hY_N⟩
    refine ⟨fun A' hA' hA'F => ?_, fun C hC hCF => ?_⟩
    · /- Any angle in that segment is the angle BAD [III. 21]. -/
      rw [angle_symm hFB hBD.symm, hDBF,
        Prop21 ⟨O, hO⟩ hA hB hD hA' (OppositeSidesOf.sameSideOf hAF.symm hA'F.symm)]
    -- Next, since ABCD is a quadrilateral in a circle,
    -- its opposite angles are equal to two right angles. [III. 22]
    have h22 := (Prop22 ⟨O, hO⟩ hA hB hC hD (hCF.trans_opposite hAF.symm).symm).2
    -- But the angles DBF, DBE are also equal to two right angles;
    have h13 : ∠ F B D + ∠ D B E = ∟ + ∟ :=
      BookI.Prop13 (between_symm hEBF) (fun ⟨K, hF_K, hE_K, hD_K⟩ =>
        hD_L ((line_unique (ne_of_between_ends hEBF).symm hF_K hE_K hF_L hE_L) ▸ hD_K))
    -- therefore the angles DBF, DBE are equal to the angles BAD, BCD,
    rw [angle_symm hFB hBD.symm, ← h22] at h13
    -- of which the angle BAD was proved equal to the angle DBF;
    rw [hDBF] at h13
    -- therefore the angle DBE which remains is equal to the angle DCB in the alternate segment
    -- DCB of the circle.
    have hEB : E ≠ B := ne_of_between hEBF
    rw [add_comm (∠ B A D), add_comm (∠ B A D)] at h13
    rw [angle_symm hEB hBD.symm]
    exact CommonNotion3 h13 rfl
  -- Therefore etc.
  have hEF_BD : OppositeSidesOf E F B D :=
    (OppositeSidesOf.of_between (Triangle.of_line hB_L hE_L (ne_of_between hEBF).symm hD_L).cab
      hEBF).swap
  by_cases hDA : D = A
  · /- When D is A, BD is the diameter: both segments are semicircles, and every angle
       in them is right by III.31, as are the angles FBD, EBD. -/
    subst hDA
    have hBOD : Between B O D := between_symm hAOB
    refine ⟨fun A' hA' hA'F => ?_, fun C hC hCF => ?_⟩
    · have hT := hA'F.triangle
      rw [angle_symm (ne_of_between (between_symm hEBF)) hBD.symm, hright hF_L
        (ne_of_between (between_symm hEBF))]
      exact ((Prop31 hO hA' hB hD hBOD hT.ne₁₃.symm hT.ne₂₃.symm).1).symm
    · have hT := hCF.triangle
      rw [angle_symm (ne_of_between hEBF) hBD.symm, hright hE_L (ne_of_between hEBF)]
      exact ((Prop31 hO hC hD hB hAOB hT.ne₂₃.symm hT.ne₁₃.symm).1).symm
  · have hDBA : ¬ OnLine D M := fun h =>
      (Prop2.triangle ⟨O, hO⟩ hD hB hA hBD.symm hAB.symm hDA) ⟨M, h, hB_M, hA_M⟩
    have hA_L : ¬ OnLine A L := off hA hAB
    have hEF_BA : OppositeSidesOf E F B A :=
      (OppositeSidesOf.of_between (Triangle.of_line hB_L hE_L (ne_of_between hEBF).symm hA_L).cab
        hEBF).swap
    by_cases hs : SameSideOf D F B A
    · exact key hEBF hE_L hF_L hs
    · have hDF : OppositeSidesOf D F B A :=
        OppositeSidesOf.of_line hAB.symm hB_M hA_M
          ⟨hDBA, fun h => hEF_BA.2 M hB_M hA_M |>.2.1 h,
            fun h => hs (SameSideOf.of_line hAB.symm hB_M hA_M h)⟩
      obtain ⟨k₁, k₂⟩ := key (between_symm hEBF) hF_L hE_L
        (OppositeSidesOf.sameSideOf hDF.symm hEF_BA.symm)
      refine ⟨fun A' hA' hA'F => ?_, fun C hC hCF => ?_⟩
      · have hT := hA'F.triangle
        rw [k₂ A' hA' (OppositeSidesOf.sameSideOf hA'F.symm hEF_BD.symm)]
        exact angle_symm hT.ne₂₃ hT.ne₁₃
      · have hT := hCF.triangle
        rw [k₁ C hC (hCF.trans_opposite hEF_BD.symm)]
        exact angle_symm hT.ne₁₃ hT.ne₂₃
  -- Q. E. D.
```

- [`between_cases`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Diagram.lean#L73) (through [`Prop2.triangle`](../../Elements/BookIII/Prop02.lean#L136)): Of three different points on a straight line, one is between the other two. (Between 6)
- [`between_of_between_left`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Diagram.lean#L65): If B is between A and C, and D is between A and B, then D is between A and C. (Between 4)
- [`between_of_between_right`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Diagram.lean#L69): If B is between A and C, and C is between B and D, then B is between A and D. (Between 5)
- [`between_of_inside_chord`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Diagram.lean#L146): A straight line through a point inside a circle has that point between the points where it meets the circle. (Circle 1)
- [`between_symm`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Diagram.lean#L42) (used here): If B is between A and C, it is between C and A. (Between 1)
- [`centre_inside`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Diagram.lean#L34) (used here): The centre of a circle is inside it. (Generalities 3)
- [`circles_meet`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Diagram.lean#L176): If each circle passes through a point inside the other, the circles cut one another. This is the step Euclid takes for granted in I.1. (Intersection 5)
- [`circles_meet_of_on_inside_outside`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Diagram.lean#L170): Two circles cut one another if the first passes through a point A inside the second, and a point B outside the second is inside or on the first. (Intersection 4, in LeanEuclid's corrected form)
- [`circles_meet_same_side`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Constructions.lean#L94): Two circles that cut one another do so on each side of the straight line through their centres. (Intersections 8)
- [`exists_centre`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Constructions.lean#L72): Every circle has a centre. A rule of our own, not one of System E's: its content is Euclid's Definitions I.15 and I.16.

- [`exists_point_same_side`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Constructions.lean#L45): Let a point be taken on the same side of L as B. (Points 5)
- [`inside_not_on`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Diagram.lean#L37) (through [`Prop2.triangle`](../../Elements/BookIII/Prop02.lean#L136) and [`ne_of_centre_of_on`](../../Elements/Figure/Circles.lean#L203)): A point inside a circle is not on it. (Generalities 4)
- [`line_circle_between`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Constructions.lean#L82): A straight line through a point B inside a circle, heading out to a point C outside it, cuts the circle between B and C. (Intersections 4)
- [`line_circle_beyond`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Constructions.lean#L88) (used here): A straight line through a point B inside a circle, produced beyond B away from C, cuts the circle there. (Intersections 5)

- [`ne_of_between`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Diagram.lean#L45) (used here): A point between two others differs from the first. (Between 1)
- [`ne_of_between_ends`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Diagram.lean#L48) (used here): The ends of a finite straight line differ. (Between 1)
- [`not_between_of_between`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Diagram.lean#L51): If B is between A and C, then A is not between B and C. (Between 1)
- [`not_between_of_between_between`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Diagram.lean#L78): If B is between A and C, and also between A and D, then B is not between C and D: C and D lie on the same side of B. (Between 7)
- [`not_on_line_of_same_side`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Diagram.lean#L91) (used here): Points on one side of a straight line are not on it. (Same side 3)
- [`on_line_of_between`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Diagram.lean#L55) (through [`OppositeSidesOf.of_between`](../../Elements/Figure/Sides.lean#L98)): A straight line through A and B, with B between A and C, passes through C. (Between 2)
- [`on_line_of_between_ends`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Diagram.lean#L60) (used here): A straight line through A and C passes through every point between them. (Between 3)
- [`pasch2`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Diagram.lean#L110) (through [`crossbar`](../../Elements/Figure/Angles.lean#L130)): If B is between A and C, A is on L and B is off it, then B and C are on the same side of L: a straight line that leaves L at A does not cross it again. (Pasch 2)
- [`pasch3`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Diagram.lean#L113) (used here): A straight line through a point between A and C separates them. (Pasch 3)
- [`pasch4`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Diagram.lean#L118) (through [`OppositeSides.exists_between`](../../Elements/Figure/Sides.lean#L117) and [`crossbar`](../../Elements/Figure/Angles.lean#L130)): If two different straight lines L and M meet at B, and A and C are points of M, different from each other and from B, that are not on the same side of L, then B is between A and C. (Pasch 4)
- [`same_side_or`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Diagram.lean#L98) (through [`OppositeSidesOf.sameSideOf`](../../Elements/Figure/Sides.lean#L127)): A straight line has only two sides. (Same side 5)
- [`same_side_refl`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Diagram.lean#L84) (through [`OppositeSides.exists_between`](../../Elements/Figure/Sides.lean#L117)): A point off a straight line is on the same side of it as itself. (Same side 1)
- [`same_side_symm`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Diagram.lean#L88) (used here): If A is on the same side of a straight line as B, then B is on the same side as A. (Same side 2)
- [`same_side_trans`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Diagram.lean#L95) (used here): Two points on the same side of a straight line as a third point are on the same side as each other. (Same side 4)
- [`triple_incidence1`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Diagram.lean#L130) (through [`crossbar`](../../Elements/Figure/Angles.lean#L130)): Take B on L, C on M and D on N, three straight lines through A. If C lies within the angle BAD (on D's side of L and on B's side of N), then B and D are not on the same side of M: the straight line AC separates them. (Triple incidence 1)
- [`triple_incidence2`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Diagram.lean#L138): Take B on L, C on M and D on N, three straight lines through A, with B other than A and D off M. If C and D are on the same side of L, and B and D are not on the same side of M, then B and C are on the same side of N: C lies within the angle BAD. (Triple incidence 2)

**Lengths, angles and areas**

- [`angle_add_of_inside`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Transfer.lean#L55) (through [`angle_add_of_within`](../../Elements/Figure/Angles.lean#L68)): If D lies within the angle BAC, then BAC is made up of BAD and DAC. (Diagram-angle 2)
- [`angle_eq_of_same_rays`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Transfer.lean#L62) (through [`angle_onRay_right`](../../Elements/Figure/Angles.lean#L47)): The angle doesn't change if its arms are traced through other points on the same rays. (Diagram-angle 4)
- [`angle_symm`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Metric.lean#L26) (used here): The angle ABC is the angle CBA. (Metric 4)
- [`area_congruent`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Metric.lean#L43): Triangles equal in all their sides and angles are equal in area. Euclid uses this without comment once he has shown two triangles congruent. (Metric 9)
- [`area_rotate`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Metric.lean#L35): The triangle ABC is the triangle CAB. (Metric 8)
- [`area_swap`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Metric.lean#L38): The triangle ABC is the triangle ACB. (Metric 8)
- [`eq_of_len_eq_zero`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Metric.lean#L17): A finite straight line with distinct ends has length. (Metric 1)
- [`inside_of_len_lt`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Transfer.lean#L34): A point nearer the centre than the circumference is inside. (Diagram-segment 4)
- [`len_add_of_between`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Transfer.lean#L22): If B is between A and C, then AB and BC together make up AC. (Diagram-segment 1)
- [`len_lt_of_inside`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Transfer.lean#L38): A point inside is nearer the centre than the circumference. (Diagram-segment 4)
- [`len_self`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Metric.lean#L20): The "straight line" from a point to itself has no length. (Metric 1)
- [`len_symm`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Metric.lean#L23): The straight line AB is the straight line BA. (Metric 3)
- [`same_ray_of_angle_eq_zero`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Transfer.lean#L50): If the angle BAC is nothing, C lies on the ray from A through B. (Diagram-angle 1)

**Superposition**

- [`superposition`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Superposition.lean#L30): **Superposition.** The triangle ABC can be applied to the straight line L with A on D, B on the ray from D through G, and C on the side of L where H is, without changing any side or angle.

**Laws of magnitude**

- [`add_assoc`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Magnitudes.lean#L23) (used here): Adding three magnitudes in a row, it makes no difference whether the first two or the last two are added first. (System E §3.5)
- [`add_comm`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Magnitudes.lean#L26) (used here): The order of adding does not matter. (System E §3.5)
- [`add_lt_add_right`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Magnitudes.lean#L45): Adding the same thing to both sides keeps "less than". (System E §3.5)
- [`add_zero`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Magnitudes.lean#L29): Adding nothing changes nothing. (System E §3.5)
- [`lt_irrefl`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Magnitudes.lean#L32): No magnitude is less than itself. (System E §3.5)
- [`lt_trans`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Magnitudes.lean#L35): What is less than the less is less still. (System E §3.5)
- [`lt_trichotomy`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Magnitudes.lean#L39): Of two magnitudes, one is less, or they are equal, or the other is less. (System E §3.5)
- [`not_lt_zero`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Magnitudes.lean#L42): Nothing is less than zero. (System E §3.5)

</details>

## Mishnah

_Our commentary: what Euclid assumes, what Lean made us say out loud, and how the result looks by modern means._

Euclid's key is a diameter. BA, at right angles to the tangent, passes through the centre (III.19), and the angle ADB in the semicircle is right (III.31), so the angles ABD, BAD of the triangle make a right angle, as ABF does. Take the common ABD away, and DBF is left equal to BAD. His A is the end of the diameter, but we may take any angle in the segment BAD, for they are all equal (III.21).

**A test for touching.** Heath states the converse (vol. 2, p. 66): a straight line through B making with BD angles equal to those in the alternate segments touches the circle. He gives Christopher Clavius' direct proof (p. 67), Euclid's run backwards: add ABD to the equal angles FBD, BAD, and ABF equals ABD and BAD together, a right angle, so EF touches the circle by the porism to III.16. The equal angles test for contact as well as follow from it.

Pappus, Heath reports, assumes a consequence of III.32: "*If two circles touch, any straight line drawn through the point of contact and terminated by both circles cuts off segments in each which are respectively similar*" (vol. 2, p. 67). Pappus proves it with the common tangent there: the straight line makes equal angles with it in the two circles, so by III.32 the angles in their alternate segments are equal, and the segments are similar (Definition III.11).

**Which side is the circle on?** In Euclid's figure the whole circle except B lies on one side of EF, and he never says why. The reason is III.18's: a straight line that touches has no point within the circle, so it cannot part two points of it (`Prop32.sameSide`). The figure also puts D on F's side of BA; otherwise we exchange E and F. When BD is itself the diameter, every angle in either segment is right (III.31), as are the angles at B: a case Euclid never separates, for, as Heath remarks under III.33, it too would need III.31.

**The modern way.** On the circle $|z| = 1$ in the complex plane, the tangent at B runs in the direction $i\mathrm{B}$. Turn B about the centre through $\theta$, with $0 \lt \theta \lt 2\pi$, to $\mathrm{D} = \mathrm{B}e^{i\theta}$. Then $\mathrm{D} - \mathrm{B} = 2\sin(\theta/2) \thinspace i\mathrm{B}e^{i\theta/2}$, which is $i\mathrm{B}$ turned through $\theta/2$ and multiplied by a positive number, so the tangent makes with BD the angle $\theta/2$: the angle at the circumference standing on the arc BD that $\theta$ sweeps.

## Further reading

- Isaac Todhunter calls the converse "true and important": a straight line making with BD the angles in the alternate segments touches the circle. His note on III.32 (p. 277) is in [*The Elements of Euclid*](https://archive.org/details/todhuntereuclid00todhrich) (1872, free online) (also on [III.3](03.md)).
- Two touching circles cut by straight lines through the point of contact fill Props. 2–4 of Book III, Section I (pp. 29–30), in John Casey's [*A Sequel to the First Six Books of the Elements of Euclid*](https://archive.org/details/sequeltofirstsix00caserich) (1886, free online), each proved with the common tangent and III.32, as Pappus proves his (also on [III.17](17.md)).
- Evan Chen's olympiad course, [*Euclidean Geometry in Mathematical Olympiads*](https://doi.org/10.5948/9781614444114) (2016), works on the circle |z| = 1, as the modern way does, in §6.4, "The Unit Circle" (pp. 100–102) (also on [III.24](24.md)).
